terms.meaning: the bundle of project data the server sends to this page.

sections.name: File setup, ProjectPage
sections.title: Imports and page names
sections.what: Loads the needed libraries, shared pieces, citation helper, lifecycle labels and data types, and defines the two page names, news and profiles.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These are the parts the page needs to load data, show it and open citations.
sections.watch_out: Any page name other than news shows the profiles page, so a typo quietly shows the wrong page.

sections.name: KIND_LABEL, ORIGIN_LABEL, KEY_LABEL, ROLE_LABEL
sections.title: Readable labels for codes
sections.what: Turns internal codes for event types, origins and key-project tests into plain English. Also holds the explanation of what makes a key project.
sections.why: Likely reason: the data uses short codes, and users should see plain words.
sections.watch_out: A new code added to the data without a label here will show as raw text. The explanation must match the real rule for key projects.

sections.name: fmtDate, money, Scope, EMPTY
sections.title: Date, money and filter shape helpers
sections.what: Shows dates at the precision the source gives, such as a quarter or just a year, and shows money in millions or billions. Also defines the shape of the scope filter.
sections.why: Likely reason: sources often give only a year or quarter, so showing a full day would make the date look more certain than it is.
sections.watch_out: A missing currency is shown as US dollars. Money values are read as millions unless they are one thousand or more, so the unit of stored values matters.

sections.name: inScope, opts
sections.title: Search and filter matching
sections.what: Decides whether a project or news item matches the chosen region, country, industry and free-text search. Search looks at name, segment, country and any extra text such as a headline or company names.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared rule keeps the news and profile pages filtering the same way.
sections.watch_out: Region, country and industry must match exactly, so differently spelled values will not match even if they mean the same place.

sections.name: ScopeBar
sections.title: Filter bar
sections.what: Shows the search box, region, country and industry dropdowns, any extra filter passed in, and a reset button. Choosing a region clears the country.
sections.why: Likely reason: a country outside the chosen region would make no sense, so the country is cleared when the region changes.
sections.watch_out: The country choices come only from the projects on the page, so the list changes as other filters change.

sections.name: SourceButton
sections.title: Source button
sections.what: Shows a small button with the publisher or site name and the publication date. Clicking it opens the full source or citation.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It sits next to each claim so users can check it.
sections.watch_out: If a source has no valid web address, building the site name will fail and can break that row.

sections.name: NewsRow
sections.title: One news row
sections.what: Draws one dated event with its type, origin, headline, project link, industry, country and source button. Marks events that are still upcoming.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared row keeps the news lists and project details looking the same.
sections.watch_out: The date shown depends on the source precision, so a year-only date may be read as more exact than it is.

sections.name: useCitations
sections.title: Opening a source
sections.what: Decides how a source opens when clicked: a full evidence citation when an evidence id exists, or a basic source view built from the web address and quote otherwise.
sections.why: Likely reason: some sources live in the evidence library and others are only web links.
sections.watch_out: The two routes show different amounts of detail, so a source with missing fields may open a thinner view.

sections.name: ProjectPages
sections.title: Main wrapper for both project pages
sections.what: Loads the project feed with a five-minute cache, shows a loading message, and shows an error message with a retry button. Then applies the starting filters, which the demo can preset, and shows the news or profiles page with an optional hint.
sections.why: Likely reason: loads data once and gives it to both pages, and the cache avoids reloading on every visit.
sections.watch_out: Data can be up to five minutes old, so a change on the server may not show until the cache expires or the user retries. Part of this section is cut off in the packet.

sections.name: NewsPage
sections.title: News page
sections.what: Shows two lists: latest dated project news, with an event-type filter, and upcoming milestones sorted soonest first. Empty messages explain that only recorded event dates appear.
sections.why: Likely reason: news dates come only from recorded events, so a source's publish date is never shown as an event date.
sections.watch_out: The heading says newest first, but this component does not sort the latest list, so the order depends on the data as it arrives.

sections.name: ProfilesPage
sections.title: Key projects page
sections.what: Lists key projects that match the chosen test and filters, sorted by how many tests they pass, then by evidence count and name. Shows the selected project's full profile beside the list.
sections.why: Likely reason: projects that meet more tests come first so the most important ones are seen first.
sections.watch_out: If the selected project drops out of the filtered list, the page quietly shows the first project instead, which can look like a different choice was made.

sections.name: Fact
sections.title: Labelled fact line
sections.what: Shows one label and value in a profile, or the words Not recorded when the value is missing.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It keeps missing information visibly marked instead of blank.
sections.watch_out: An empty text value is treated as missing, so a real but blank value shows as Not recorded.

sections.name: ProfileDetail
sections.title: Project profile detail
sections.what: Shows one project's summary, key tests, stage, capacity, planned and actual capex, key dates, technology, delay, values reported by sources (merged so one value lists all its sources), companies grouped by role, sourced delivery facts, and news in the window.
sections.why: Likely reason: gathers everything known about a project in one place, with each claim linked to its source.
sections.watch_out: The label Actual completion or Updated completion depends on a text match against the stage name, so a stage spelled differently may show the wrong label.

summary: Provides the project news page and the key project profile page, with search and filters, sourced facts, and links back to each source.
purpose: Lets users follow what is happening at key projects and check every claim against its source.
why: Likely reason: project news and profiles are built from several kinds of records, and every claim must link to evidence, so one shared structure handles both pages.
how: Loads the project feed once and caches it for five minutes, shows loading and error states with a retry button, applies shared filters, and shows either the news page or the profiles page. Dates are shown at the precision the source supports. Clicking a source opens a full citation when one exists, or a basic source view otherwise.
inputs: The project feed from the server, the page to show, optional starting filters and an optional project to open first, and an optional hint message.
outputs: A news page with latest events and upcoming milestones, or a profiles page with a list of key projects and one project's details. Source buttons open citation panels.
risks: The feed may be up to five minutes old during a session. Invalid web addresses can break the source button. Only event dates count, so a gap in the news means no event is recorded, not that nothing happened.
debug: If the page is empty, check the region, country, industry and search filters, then whether the feed loaded. If a source will not open, check its address and whether it has an evidence id. If news order looks wrong, check the order the server sends, since this component does not sort the latest news. If a label shows raw text, a new code may be missing from the label lists.
